Hey everyone! My name is Arianna, and I am an 18 year old who loves to work with tech!

So here's Knock: What if you could control your Mac without touching the keyboard?

Now you can. Hit your MacBook, and Knock runs the action you’ve assigned it to. You can switch tabs, move between desktops, play or pause your media, open any app, take a screenshot, or fire off your own custom scripts with the terminal.

If you want to see how it works before committing to anything, there’s a demo run inside the app. It shows you how taps can turn into real triggers.

01 how it works

## three knocks is a vocabulary. [...] 04 actions

## one knock, almost anything.

copy paste cut undo redo save ai accept ai reject screenshot screenshot selection play / pause next track volume mute lock screen spotlight mission control tile window switch desktop open app open url run shortcut keyboard shortcut shell command applescript+ 20 more

new: custom knock sounds. pick from a built-in library or drop in your own — a thud, a click, a coin, whatever feels right. the app plays it back when it fires, so you actually hear the knock land.

05 install

## four steps, then knock.

1.   download mactap-2.1.2 from the v2.1.2 release.
2.   unzip and drag mactap into applications.
3.   open it from applications (or spotlight).
4.   allow accessibility when asked. only the actions need it; knock detection works either way. [...] does it work offline? is it private?
yes to both. knocks are classified on-device and nothing ever gets uploaded. no account, no analytics, no network calls.

why the accessibility permission?
only the actions need it — copy, paste, keystrokes, scripts. knock detection works either way, so you can deny it and still knock.

does it drain the battery?
no. it's a small native swift menu bar app — no electron, no daemons. the sensor path sips power.

is it free?
yes, and mit open source. over five thousand people grabbed it in the first four hours.
